q: Matter is used to cover all the substances and materials from which the _____ is composed.
e: Matter is used to cover all the substances and materials from which the physical universe is composed. Physical universe is the idea that completes this fact. Chemical universe would fill a different blank than physical universe.

q: Nowadays, there is a fourth state of matter known as _____ which is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles.
e: Nowadays, there is a fourth state of matter known as plasma which is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles. Plasma is the idea that completes this fact. Colloid would fill a different blank than plasma.

q: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with _____ forces between one another.
e: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with strong forces between one another. In a solid, particles are packed tightly with strong forces, so the shape is fixed. Moderate would fill a different blank than strong.

q: Solids have a definite _____ and volume.
e: Solids have a definite shape and volume. Shape is the idea that completes this fact. Mass would fill a different blank than shape.

q: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together _____ than those in gases.
e: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together more strongly than those in gases. More strongly is the idea that completes this fact. More weakly would fill a different blank than more strongly.

q: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of _____ attractive forces between gaseous particles.
e: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of weak attractive forces between gaseous particles. In a gas, particles are far apart, move fast, and have weak attractions. Strong would fill a different blank than weak.

q: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from _____ with the gas or liquid particles.
e: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from collisions with the gas or liquid particles. Collisions is the idea that completes this fact. Attractions would fill a different blank than collisions.

q: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of _____ substance.
e: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of another substance. Another is the idea that completes this fact. A solid would fill a different blank than another.

q: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the _____.
e: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact. Volume would fill a different blank than temperature.

q: The bigger the mass, the _____ the particles diffuse.
e: The bigger the mass, the slower the particles diffuse. Slower is the idea that completes this fact. Faster would fill a different blank than slower.

q: The smaller the mass, the _____ the particles diffuse.
e: The smaller the mass, the faster the particles diffuse. Faster is the idea that completes this fact. Steadier would fill a different blank than faster.

q: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse _____.
e: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse faster. Faster is the idea that completes this fact. Randomly would fill a different blank than faster.

q: Unlike gases, solids cannot be compressed and do not _____.
e: Unlike gases, solids cannot be compressed and do not flow. Flow is the idea that completes this fact. Vibrate is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Solids do expand _____ when heated.
e: Solids do expand slightly when heated. Slightly is the idea that completes this fact. Rapidly would fill a different blank than slightly.

q: Liquids can take up the shape of the container because particles are able to move _____ throughout the liquids.
e: Liquids can take up the shape of the container because particles are able to move freely throughout the liquids. Freely is the idea that completes this fact. Slowly would fill a different blank than freely.

q: The gas in a container spreads out to occupy the whole space of the container taking its shape and _____.
e: The gas in a container spreads out to occupy the whole space of the container taking its shape and volume. Volume is the idea that completes this fact. Density would fill a different blank than volume.

q: Diffusion is mainly seen in _____ and gases.
e: Diffusion is mainly seen in liquids and gases. Liquids is the idea that completes this fact. Plasmas would fill a different blank than liquids.

q: Plasma is a hot _____ gas containing charged particles.
e: Plasma is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles. Ionised is the idea that completes this fact. Magnetic would fill a different blank than ionised.

q: When a few drops of perfume are released into a room, the particles of perfume move through the air and _____ the room.
e: When a few drops of perfume are released into a room, the particles of perfume move through the air and spread the room. Spread is the idea that completes this fact. Cool would fill a different blank than spread.

q: Preparing tea using a tea bag in hot water is an example of _____ in daily life.
e: Preparing tea using a tea bag in hot water is an example of diffusion in daily life. Diffusion is the spreading of particles from higher to lower concentration. Filtration would fill a different blank than diffusion.

q: The motion of pollen grains on still water is an example of _____ motion.
e: The motion of pollen grains on still water is an example of Brownian motion. Brownian motion is the random jiggling of tiny particles hit by fast molecules in a fluid. Rotary would fill a different blank than Brownian.

q: Mercury and bromine are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Mercury and bromine are examples of elements that are liquids at room temperature. Liquids is the idea that completes this fact. Gases would fill a different blank than liquids.

q: Oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and chlorine are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and chlorine are examples of elements that are gases at room temperature. Gases is the idea that completes this fact. Solids would fill a different blank than gases.

q: Copper, iron, zinc, silver, gold, carbon and phosphorus are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Copper, iron, zinc, silver, gold, carbon and phosphorus are examples of elements that are solids at room temperature. Solids is the idea that completes this fact. Liquids would fill a different blank than solids.

q: Metals have _____ density compared to non-metals.
e: Metals have high density compared to non-metals. High is the idea that completes this fact. Low would fill a different blank than high.

q: A physical change is a change in which no _____ substances are formed.
e: A physical change is a change in which no new substances are formed. New is the idea that completes this fact. Gaseous would fill a different blank than new.

q: The temperature at which a solid melts is called the _____ point.
e: The temperature at which a solid melts is called the melting point. Melting is solid to liquid as particles gain energy and leave their fixed places. Freezing would fill a different blank than melting.

q: Vaporisation is the process that occurs when a chemical or element is converted from a liquid to a _____.
e: Vaporisation is the process that occurs when a chemical or element is converted from a liquid to a vapour. Vapour is the gas form of a substance that is usually liquid, made by vaporisation. Plasma would fill a different blank than vapour.

q: Evaporation is the process of a substance in a liquid state changing to a gaseous state due to an increase in _____ and / or pressure.
e: Evaporation is the process of a substance in a liquid state changing to a gaseous state due to an increase in temperature and / or pressure. Raising temperature or lowering pressure helps a liquid evaporate. Density would fill a different blank than temperature.

q: Boiling is the rapid vaporisation of a liquid, which occurs when a liquid is heated to its _____ point.
e: Boiling is the rapid vaporisation of a liquid, which occurs when a liquid is heated to its boiling point. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point. Freezing would fill a different blank than boiling.

q: Sublimation is the change of solid state directly into gaseous state without _____.
e: Sublimation is the change of solid state directly into gaseous state without melting. Melting is solid to liquid as particles gain energy and leave their fixed places. Cooling would fill a different blank than melting.

q: Deposition is the direct solidification of a vapour by _____.
e: Deposition is the direct solidification of a vapour by cooling. Cooling is the idea that completes this fact. Heating would fill a different blank than cooling.

q: A chemical change is a change in which one or more _____ substances are formed.
e: A chemical change is a change in which one or more new substances are formed. New is the idea that completes this fact. Old would fill a different blank than new.

q: Heating of limestone or marble is an example of a chemical change known as _____.
e: Heating of limestone or marble is an example of a chemical change known as dissociation. Dissociation is the idea that completes this fact. Precipitation would fill a different blank than dissociation.

q: Use of magnesia to treat gastric patient is an example of a chemical change known as _____.
e: Use of magnesia to treat gastric patient is an example of a chemical change known as neutralisation. Neutralisation is acid plus base making salt and water. Dissociation would fill a different blank than neutralisation.

q: Passing carbon dioxide into lime water is an example of a chemical change known as _____.
e: Passing carbon dioxide into lime water is an example of a chemical change known as precipitation. Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid from a solution. Dissociation would fill a different blank than precipitation.

q: Melting, boiling, freezing, evaporation, vaporisation, condensation and sublimation are considered as _____ changes.
e: Melting, boiling, freezing, evaporation, vaporisation, condensation and sublimation are considered as physical changes. A physical change does not make a new substance; melting and boiling are typical examples. Chemical would fill a different blank than physical.

q: When a solid substance is heated, the particles of the solid vibrate more _____.
e: When a solid substance is heated, the particles of the solid vibrate more strongly. Strongly is the idea that completes this fact. Slowly would fill a different blank than strongly.

q: Eventually, the particles have enough energy to completely break the forces holding them together, and a _____ is formed.
e: Eventually, the particles have enough energy to completely break the forces holding them together, and a gas is formed. In a gas, particles are far apart, move fast, and have weak attractions. Solid would fill a different blank than gas.

q: Iodine solid changes to iodine vapour, where heat is absorbed. This is known as _____.
e: Iodine solid changes to iodine vapour, where heat is absorbed. This is known as sublimation. Sublimation is solid going straight to gas, or the reverse, without a liquid stage. Vaporisation would fill a different blank than sublimation.

q: Water vapour turns to frost is an example of _____.
e: Water vapour turns to frost is an example of deposition. Deposition is the idea that completes this fact. Sublimation would fill a different blank than deposition.

q: Cooking of rice from rice grains, green mangoes ripening, and burning of a match are examples of _____ changes.
e: Cooking of rice from rice grains, green mangoes ripening, and burning of a match are examples of chemical changes. A chemical change makes new substances, like burning or cooking rice. Physical would fill a different blank than chemical.

q: Mothballs sublime into vapour of deodorant for toilets and bathrooms. It is also a _____ change.
e: Mothballs sublime into vapour of deodorant for toilets and bathrooms. It is also a physical change. A physical change does not make a new substance; melting and boiling are typical examples. Chemical would fill a different blank than physical.

q: Iron rusting and vegetables rotting are examples of _____ changes in daily life.
e: Iron rusting and vegetables rotting are examples of chemical changes in daily life. A chemical change makes new substances, like burning or cooking rice. Reversible would fill a different blank than chemical.

q: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid is equal to the atmospheric pressure of the surrounding is called the _____ point.
e: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid is equal to the atmospheric pressure of the surrounding is called the boiling point. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point. Melting would fill a different blank than boiling.

q: Freezing is the process in which a liquid becomes sufficiently cold to change into a _____.
e: Freezing is the process in which a liquid becomes sufficiently cold to change into a solid. Solid is the idea that completes this fact. Plasma would fill a different blank than solid.

q: Condensation is the change from a _____ state to its liquid state.
e: Condensation is the change from a gaseous state to its liquid state. Gaseous is the idea that completes this fact. Solid would fill a different blank than gaseous.

q: In a physical change, there may be a temporary change in colour, temperature and state, but no _____ substances are formed.
e: In a physical change, there may be a temporary change in colour, temperature and state, but no new substances are formed. New is the idea that completes this fact. Pure would fill a different blank than new.

q: Dissolving sugar in water is an example of a _____ change.
e: Dissolving sugar in water is an example of a physical change. A physical change does not make a new substance; melting and boiling are typical examples. Nuclear would fill a different blank than physical.

q: Photosynthesis reaction and making soaps and detergents are examples of _____ changes.
e: Photosynthesis reaction and making soaps and detergents are examples of chemical changes. A chemical change makes new substances, like burning or cooking rice. Physical would fill a different blank than chemical.

q: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and _____.
e: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary. Compounds would fill a different blank than mixtures.

q: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant _____.
e: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant composition. Composition is the idea that completes this fact. Volume would fill a different blank than composition.

q: At the beginning of the 19th century, _____ proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms.
e: At the beginning of the 19th century, John Dalton proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms. Dalton treated atoms as the tiny particles that make up elements. Albert Einstein would fill a different blank than John Dalton.

q: Elements are substances consisting of _____ type of atom.
e: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom. One is the idea that completes this fact. Two would fill a different blank than one.

q: There are _____ known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined state.
e: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined state. 92 is the idea that completes this fact. 82 would fill a different blank than 92.

q: Metals show metallic luster, whereas non-metals do not show metallic _____.
e: Metals show metallic luster, whereas non-metals do not show metallic luster. Luster is the idea that completes this fact. Conductivity is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Most of the metals are malleable and ductile, while non-metals are usually _____.
e: Most of the metals are malleable and ductile, while non-metals are usually brittle. Brittle is the idea that completes this fact. Ductile would fill a different blank than brittle.

q: A molecule of an element consists of atoms of the _____ kind.
e: A molecule of an element consists of atoms of the same kind. Same is the idea that completes this fact. Multiple would fill a different blank than same.

q: A molecule of a compound consists of more than _____ kind of atoms.
e: A molecule of a compound consists of more than one kind of atoms. One is the idea that completes this fact. Two would fill a different blank than one.

q: A hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a _____ molecule.
e: A hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a diatomic molecule. Diatomic is the idea that completes this fact. Polyatomic would fill a different blank than diatomic.

q: Water is formed by combining two different elements, so it is a triatomic molecule or a _____ compound.
e: Water is formed by combining two different elements, so it is a triatomic molecule or a binary compound. Binary is the idea that completes this fact. Quaternary would fill a different blank than binary.

q: Ethanol is a polyatomic molecule formed from three different elements, so it is a _____ compound.
e: Ethanol is a polyatomic molecule formed from three different elements, so it is a ternary compound. Ternary is the idea that completes this fact. Quaternary would fill a different blank than ternary.

q: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not _____ combined.
e: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not chemically combined. Chemically is the idea that completes this fact. Gravitationally is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Brass is a solid-solid _____ mixture of the elements copper and zinc.
e: Brass is a solid-solid homogeneous mixture of the elements copper and zinc. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution. Colloidal would fill a different blank than homogeneous.

q: A mixture of flour and rice powder is an example of a solid-solid _____ mixture.
e: A mixture of flour and rice powder is an example of a solid-solid heterogeneous mixture. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts. Homogeneous would fill a different blank than heterogeneous.

q: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a _____.
e: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact. Gas would fill a different blank than liquid.

q: In filtration, the water that passes through the filter paper is called the _____.
e: In filtration, the water that passes through the filter paper is called the filtrate. Filtrate is the idea that completes this fact. Solute would fill a different blank than filtrate.

q: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid _____ state.
e: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid crystalline state. Crystalline is the idea that completes this fact. Amorphous would fill a different blank than crystalline.

q: Decanting is just allowing a mixture of solid and liquid or two immiscible liquids to settle and separate by _____.
e: Decanting is just allowing a mixture of solid and liquid or two immiscible liquids to settle and separate by gravity. Gravity is the idea that completes this fact. Magnetism would fill a different blank than gravity.

q: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different _____ points can be separated.
e: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different boiling points can be separated. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point. Melting would fill a different blank than boiling.

q: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a _____ column.
e: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a fractionating column. A fractionating column lets a liquid mixture split into fractions with different boiling points. Chromatography would fill a different blank than fractionating.

q: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and _____ speed.
e: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and rotor speed. Rotor is the idea that completes this fact. Linear would fill a different blank than rotor.

q: Chromatography is a separation method that depends on the speed at which substances move through special media, consisting of a stationary phase and a _____ phase.
e: Chromatography is a separation method that depends on the speed at which substances move through special media, consisting of a stationary phase and a mobile phase. Mobile is the idea that completes this fact. Liquid would fill a different blank than mobile.

q: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through _____ means.
e: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through chemical means. Chemical is the idea that completes this fact. Physical would fill a different blank than chemical.

q: Every element is made up of its own type of atoms, therefore it has a unique position in the _____ Table.
e: Every element is made up of its own type of atoms, therefore it has an unique position in the Periodic Table. The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number so similar properties sit in groups. Multiplication would fill a different blank than Periodic.

q: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed _____.
e: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed ratio. Ratio is the idea that completes this fact. State would fill a different blank than ratio.

q: A molecule is the simplest unit of the chemical substance, usually a group of two or more _____.
e: A molecule is the simplest unit of the chemical substance, usually a group of two or more atoms. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact. Electrons would fill a different blank than atoms.

q: Diatomic molecules are molecules composed of only _____ atoms of same or different elements.
e: Diatomic molecules are molecules composed of only two atoms of same or different elements. Two is the idea that completes this fact. Four would fill a different blank than two.

q: Triatomic molecules are molecules composed of only _____ atoms of same or different elements.
e: Triatomic molecules are molecules composed of only three atoms of same or different elements. Three is the idea that completes this fact. Two would fill a different blank than three.

q: Polyatomic molecules are molecules composed of _____ or more atoms of same or different elements.
e: Polyatomic molecules are molecules composed of three or more atoms of same or different elements. Three is the idea that completes this fact. One would fill a different blank than three.

q: The compounds formed by the combination of two elements are called _____ compounds.
e: The compounds formed by the combination of two elements are called binary compounds. Binary is the idea that completes this fact. Ternary would fill a different blank than binary.

q: The compounds formed by the combination of three elements are called _____ compounds.
e: The compounds formed by the combination of three elements are called ternary compounds. Ternary is the idea that completes this fact. Binary would fill a different blank than ternary.

q: A heterogeneous mixture is one that is non-uniform, and where the different components of the mixture can be _____.
e: A heterogeneous mixture is one that is non-uniform, and where the different components of the mixture can be seen. Seen is the idea that completes this fact. Dissolved would fill a different blank than seen.

q: A homogeneous mixture is one in which the composition of its components are _____ mixed throughout.
e: A homogeneous mixture is one in which the composition of its components are uniformly mixed throughout. Uniformly is the idea that completes this fact. Randomly would fill a different blank than uniformly.

q: An alloy is a substance made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to _____.
e: An alloy is a substance made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion. Corrosion is the idea that completes this fact. Heat would fill a different blank than corrosion.

q: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is _____ in nature.
e: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is magnetic in nature. Magnetic is the idea that completes this fact. Radioactive would fill a different blank than magnetic.

q: Some solids such as copper(II) sulphate ($CuSO_4$), sugar and common salt are _____ in water.
e: Some solids such as copper(II) sulphate (CuSO4), sugar and common salt are soluble in water. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Insoluble would fill a different blank than soluble.

q: Some solids such as sand, charcoal and chalk are _____ in water.
e: Some solids such as sand, charcoal and chalk are insoluble in water. Insoluble is the idea that completes this fact. Soluble would fill a different blank than insoluble.

q: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions and are called _____ liquids.
e: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions and are called miscible liquids. Miscible is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible would fill a different blank than miscible.

q: Liquids that do not mix are called _____ liquids.
e: Liquids that do not mix are called immiscible liquids. Immiscible is the idea that completes this fact. Miscible is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Dry air is a familiar example of a _____ solution.
e: Dry air is a familiar example of a gaseous solution. Gaseous is the idea that completes this fact. Liquid would fill a different blank than gaseous.

q: Brass is an example of a _____ solution.
e: Brass is an example of a solid solution. Solid is the idea that completes this fact. Gaseous would fill a different blank than solid.

q: Salt water is a familiar example of a solid dissolved within a _____.
e: Salt water is a familiar example of a solid dissolved within a liquid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact. Solid would fill a different blank than liquid.

q: Carbonated water contains carbon dioxide gas molecules existing between molecules of _____.
e: Carbonated water contains carbon dioxide gas molecules existing between molecules of water. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Ethanol would fill a different blank than water.

q: Blood and saliva are some of the more familiar solutions of _____ importance.
e: Blood and saliva are some of the more familiar solutions of biological importance. Biological is the idea that completes this fact. Physical would fill a different blank than biological.

q: A solution is a _____ mixture of two or more substances.
e: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution. Heterogeneous would fill a different blank than homogeneous.

q: When sugar is mixed with water, the sugar is the _____ and water is the solvent.
e: When sugar is mixed with water, the sugar is the solute and water is the solvent. The solute is the substance that dissolves. Mixture would fill a different blank than solute.

q: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as _____ solutions.
e: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as aqueous solutions. Aqueous is the idea that completes this fact. Liquid would fill a different blank than aqueous.

q: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an _____ solution.
e: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an unsaturated solution. Unsaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Supersaturated would fill a different blank than unsaturated.

q: A _____ solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred.
e: A saturated solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred. Saturated is the idea that completes this fact. Supersaturated would fill a different blank than saturated.

q: The amount in grams of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the _____ of that solute.
e: The amount in grams of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the solubility of that solute. Solubility is the idea that completes this fact. Concentration would fill a different blank than solubility.

q: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a _____ solution.
e: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a supersaturated solution. Supersaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Saturated would fill a different blank than supersaturated.

q: When the temperature of the solution is increased, the solubility of most solutes _____.
e: When the temperature of the solution is increased, the solubility of most solutes increases. Increases is the idea that completes this fact. Decreases would fill a different blank than increases.

q: The solubility of all gases and some solids such as calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate _____ when temperature of the solution is increased.
e: The solubility of all gases and some solids such as calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate decreases when temperature of the solution is increased. Decreases is the idea that completes this fact. Increases would fill a different blank than decreases.

q: In a solution, the solute is _____ distributed throughout the solution.
e: In a solution, the solute is uniformly distributed throughout the solution. Uniformly is the idea that completes this fact. Unevenly would fill a different blank than uniformly.

q: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a _____ mixture.
e: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a homogeneous mixture. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution. Heterogeneous would fill a different blank than homogeneous.

q: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's _____.
e: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's crust. Crust is the idea that completes this fact. Core would fill a different blank than crust.

q: Nutrients are carried in water solution to all parts of a _____.
e: Nutrients are carried in water solution to all parts of a plant. Plant is the idea that completes this fact. Mineral would fill a different blank than plant.

q: Ethanol, acetic acid and sulphuric acid are _____ in water.
e: Ethanol, acetic acid and sulphuric acid are soluble in water. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible would fill a different blank than soluble.

q: Petrol and oils are _____ in water.
e: Petrol and oils are insoluble in water. Insoluble is the idea that completes this fact. Soluble would fill a different blank than insoluble.

q: Hydrogen chloride and ammonia are gases that are _____ in water.
e: Hydrogen chloride and ammonia are gases that are soluble in water. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible would fill a different blank than soluble.

q: Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are gases that are not very _____ in water.
e: Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are gases that are not very soluble in water. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate _____ g of water, at that temperature.
e: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate 100 g of water, at that temperature. 100 is the idea that completes this fact. 10 would fill a different blank than 100.

q: A solution in which more of the solute can dissolve at the given temperature is called an _____ solution.
e: A solution in which more of the solute can dissolve at the given temperature is called an unsaturated solution. Unsaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Supersaturated would fill a different blank than unsaturated.

q: The solution that retains more solute than that required to saturate the solution at room temperature is called a _____ solution.
e: The solution that retains more solute than that required to saturate the solution at room temperature is called a supersaturated solution. Supersaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Unsaturated would fill a different blank than supersaturated.

q: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases, so the excess solute will come out as a _____.
e: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases, so the excess solute will come out as a solid. Solid is the idea that completes this fact. Gas would fill a different blank than solid.

q: Wine is separated from the sediments by _____ in daily life applications.
e: Wine is separated from the sediments by decantation in daily life applications. Decantation is the idea that completes this fact. Filtration would fill a different blank than decantation.

q: Plasma can be removed from blood by decantation after _____.
e: Plasma can be removed from blood by decantation after centrifugation. Centrifugation is the idea that completes this fact. Filtration would fill a different blank than centrifugation.

q: Milk is a colloid of fat globules suspended in water, which is an example of a _____ mixture.
e: Milk is a colloid of fat globules suspended in water, which is an example of a heterogeneous mixture. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts. Pure would fill a different blank than heterogeneous.

q: Decanting a mixture containing flammable solvents can be dangerous as the flammable material evaporates and forms dangerous _____.
e: Decanting a mixture containing flammable solvents can be dangerous as the flammable material evaporates and forms dangerous fumes. Fumes is the idea that completes this fact. Solids would fill a different blank than fumes.
